DPO differs from the PPO-based RLHF pipeline used in InstructGPT in that DPO bypasses the need for fitting an explicit reward and performing reinforcement learning (RL) to learn the policy. Instead, DPO uses a single maximum likelihood objective, which allows it to optimize the parametric model directly without the complexities associated with actor-critic algorithms like PPO. Additionally, DPO's reward/KL tradeoff strictly dominates that of PPO, and it achieves better performance even when PPO has access to ground truth rewards [dpo, p.4][dpo, p.8].

Self-RAG differs from conventional RAG in that it enables retrieval on demand and selection of the best possible model output via fine-grained self-reflection. While conventional RAG processes retrieved passages in a more straightforward manner, Self-RAG concurrently processes multiple retrieved passages, evaluates their relevance, and generates corresponding task outputs. It also generates critique tokens to criticize its own output and choose the best one based on factuality and overall quality, which is not a feature of conventional RAG [self_rag, p.0].

RAPTOR differs from traditional RAG by using a recursive tree structure that captures both high-level and low-level details about a text. It clusters chunks of text, generates summaries of those clusters, and builds the tree from the bottom up. This allows RAPTOR to load into an LLM’s context chunks representing the text at different levels, enabling it to effectively and efficiently answer questions at varying levels of granularity. In contrast, traditional RAG typically does not utilize such a multi-layered structure for indexing and retrieval [raptor, p.0].

CRAG differs from conventional RAG in that it specifically addresses the issue of inaccurate results returned by the retriever and incorporates corrective strategies to improve robustness. While conventional RAG approaches indiscriminately incorporate retrieved documents regardless of their relevance, CRAG utilizes a lightweight retrieval evaluator to assess the quality of these documents and triggers different knowledge retrieval actions based on their confidence degree.
